reasoning: Recent high-quality public polls over the last ~10 days consistently show Democrat James Talarico holding a very small lead over Republican Ken Paxton in the Texas U.S. Senate race, generally in the D+2 to D+5 range, with all margins within typical polling error.[1][2][3][8][9][10][11][12][13] Structural ratings and older polling-based forecasts still show Texas leaning Republican overall, but the *current* polling environment points to a razor-thin, slightly Democratic edge in the Senate contest, best described as roughly D+2–3 on recent averages.[12][16]

sources.name: The Hill (reporting Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research & Survey Center poll)
sources.details: Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center poll of 1,200 likely voters finds Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 45%, a 2-point lead for the Democrat in the Texas Senate race.

sources.name: Bloomberg (reporting Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research & Survey Center and Fox News polls)
sources.details: Bloomberg reports the Texas Southern University/Barbara Jordan Center poll showing Talarico leading Paxton 47%-45%, with a Fox News poll also cited giving Talarico a 3-point edge.

sources.name: Fox News
sources.details: Fox News poll of 1,006 Texas registered voters shows Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 48%, a 3-point Democratic advantage within the margin of error.

sources.name: USA Today (reporting Fox News poll)
sources.details: USA Today coverage of the Fox News survey reports Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 48% in the Senate race, highlighting a narrow 3-point Democratic lead.

sources.name: USA Today (reporting Texas Public Opinion Research poll)
sources.details: Texas Public Opinion Research poll of 1,048 likely voters finds Talarico leading Paxton 45% to 40%, a 5-point edge for Democrats in the Texas Senate race.

sources.name: Punchbowl News (reporting Texas Public Opinion Research poll)
sources.details: Punchbowl News summarizes the Texas Public Opinion Research survey showing Talarico ahead of Paxton 45% to 40%, a 5-point Democratic lead with 14% undecided.

sources.name: Newsweek (reporting Texas Public Opinion Research poll and 270toWin average)
sources.details: Newsweek reports the Texas Public Opinion Research poll with Talarico at 45% and Paxton at 40%, noting a growing but modest 5-point advantage for the Democrat and referencing 270toWin’s average showing Talarico narrowly ahead.

sources.name: Axios (reporting Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research & Survey Center, Fox News, and TPOR polls)
sources.details: Axios covers the Barbara Jordan Center poll of 1,200 likely voters, finding Talarico up 47%-45%, and notes three consecutive public polls (Fox News, TPOR, Texas Southern) all showing Talarico narrowly ahead.

sources.name: Pollsmax Texas Senate Forecast
sources.details: Pollsmax’s Texas Senate forecast as of June 24 shows a polling-average margin of R+1.9 and an overall race rating of R+6.7, indicating a structurally Republican-leaning contest based on data through late June.
